places.i: The Bible's Haran lies near modern Urfa in southern Turkey. Abraham 2:4 says the land was named after Abraham's brother Haran, who died in the famine.

places.n: House of the Forest of Lebanon

places.i: The "plains of Moreh" (Abraham 2:18) is the oak or terebinth of Moreh beside Shechem (Genesis 12:6), probably a local Canaanite shrine.

The site of Abraham's Ur of the Chaldees is disputed. The most popular candidate is Tell el-Muqayyar in southern Iraq, where this point is. Some scholars propose a site on the Syrian-Turkish border, which suits the Egyptian details of Abraham 1 better (Stephen O. Smoot, Pearl of Great Price Study Edition).

Bend of the Missouri River where D&C 61 was dictated on 12 August 1831. The Joseph Smith Papers put it about a hundred miles downstream from Independence; Sidney Gilbert's copy says "about 40 miles above Chariton". That points to a site about five miles west of Miami, Saline County, perhaps the Corps of Engineers' Teteseau Bend. The river has since changed course, so the exact spot is lost.
Old Chariton, on the north bank of the Missouri River in Chariton County, where D&C 62 was received on 13 August 1831. The old town site is approximate.

Camp of Israel (Zion's Camp) campsite on the property of church member John Cooper, about four miles north of Fishing River, where D&C 105 was dictated on 22 June 1834 (Joseph Smith Papers). The headnote of D&C 105 names Fishing River. The exact site of the farm is not known.

Zion's Camp camped on a rise between two forks of Fishing River, Clay County, on 19 June 1834, when a violent storm scattered the armed men threatening the camp. D&C 105 was dictated three days later at a campsite about four miles north (see John Cooper's farm).
Where Zion's Camp was organized on 6 May 1834, when Joseph Smith's company from Kirtland joined the advance party. New Portage was a village near present-day Akron; the exact site is approximate.
Zion's Camp crossed the Wabash River by boat here on 24 May 1834 and camped just inside Illinois.
Zion's Camp passed through Paris, Edgar County, on 26 May 1834.
Zion's Camp passed through Springfield, Sangamon County, at the end of May 1834.
Zion's Camp camped near Jacksonville, Morgan County, at the end of May and the start of June 1834.
Zion's Camp reached Pittsfield, Pike County, on 3 June 1834.
Zion's Camp camped on the east bank of the Mississippi on 4 June 1834 and was ferried across to Louisiana, Missouri, on 5 June. The exact landing is approximate.
The Allred settlement on the Salt River, where Joseph Smith's and Hyrum Smith's companies of Zion's Camp joined on 8 June 1834. The site is approximate.
Hyrum Smith and Lyman Wight set out from Pontiac, Michigan Territory, on 5 May 1834 with a company that grew as it marched to join Zion's Camp.
Hyrum Smith's company forded the Illinois River at the mouth of the Fox River, Ottawa, on 22 May 1834.
Hyrum Smith's company reached Pekin on the Illinois River on 29 May 1834.
Hyrum Smith's company reached Quincy on 5 June 1834 and crossed the Mississippi into Missouri. In the winter of 1838-39 Quincy gave refuge to the Saints driven out of Missouri.
Refuge of the Saints driven out of Jackson County, 1833-36. Zion's Camp came to the county in June 1834 and D&C 105 was received there.
First camp of the Saints leaving Nauvoo, on Sugar Creek in Lee County, Iowa Territory, from 1 March 1846. The exact campsite is approximate.
Way station the pioneers founded in April 1846 in Decatur County, Iowa, to plant crops for those who followed.
Way station founded in May 1846 in Union County, Iowa, on the trail to the Missouri River.
Fur-trade fort where the 1847 pioneer company joined the Oregon Trail on its way to the Salt Lake Valley.
Landmark on the Sweetwater River passed by the 1847 pioneer company.
The broad pass over the Continental Divide crossed by the 1847 pioneer company.
Trading post reached by the 1847 pioneer company before the last stretch into the Salt Lake Valley.
The jail at Liberty, Clay County, where Joseph Smith was held in 1838–39 (D&C 121–123).
Camp of Israel on the west bank of the Missouri River, 1846–48 (D&C 136).

Also called Spring Hill, in Daviess County, Missouri (D&C 116). Joseph Smith's journal places the settlement near Lyman Wight's ferry on Grand River (Township 60, Ranges 27 and 28) and says the name Spring Hill was changed by revelation to Adam-ondi-Ahman, "the place where Adam shall come to visit his people" (May 1838). The valley where Adam is said to have gathered his posterity (D&C 107:53).

"The plains of Olaha Shinehah, or the land where Adam dwelt" (D&C 117:8). No exact site is known; it is placed near Adam-ondi-Ahman. The name resembles Shinehah (the sun) and Olea (the moon) in Joseph Smith's Book of Abraham translation (Abraham 3:13), as the Joseph Smith Papers note.
Gathering place of the Saints in Caldwell County, 1836–38 (D&C 115, 117–120).

Church headquarters 1831–38 and site of the first temple (D&C 109, 110, 137). D&C 107:1–58 comes from the 1835 expansion of the priesthood revelation; verses 60–100 were dictated at Hiram in 1831. The Joseph Smith Papers place D&C 51 here, though the Church's headnote says Thompson.
Home of John Johnson, where Joseph Smith worked on the Bible translation (D&C 65–81, 133). The earlier, 1831 text of the priesthood revelation (D&C 107:60–100) was dictated here on 11 November 1831.

Leman Copley's farm, where the Colesville Saints settled in 1831 (D&C 51, 56). D&C 51 gives Bishop Partridge directions for the Colesville Saints here; the Church's headnote says it was given at Thompson, but the Joseph Smith Papers place its dictation at Kirtland (the source names no place, so the editors infer it).
Conference of elders, January 1832 (D&C 75).
Named in 1831 as the center place of Zion in Jackson County (D&C 57:3).

The land and city of Zion, with its center place at Independence, Jackson County, designated in 1831 (D&C 57:1–3). In the revelations "Zion" also means the pure in heart and the gathering of the Saints, so not every verse below speaks of this place.
The city New Jerusalem, to be built in Missouri (D&C 28:9, 42:9, 84:2–4).
Land of Zion (D&C 57:1; 105:28).
The river on whose banks Joseph Smith received D&C 61 and 62; "the Missouri river in its decreed course" (D&C 121:33). Placed at the river along the northern edge of Jackson County.
The state of Missouri, "the land of Zion" (D&C 52:42; 57:1).
The state of Ohio.
A stop on the elders' journey to Missouri in 1831 (D&C 60:6; 61:30).
The place the elders were told to journey to before preaching two by two (D&C 60:5, 8).
A stop on the elders' journey to Missouri in 1831 (D&C 52:8).

Joseph Smith's home on the Susquehanna River (now Oakland), where much of the Book of Mormon was translated (D&C 3-13, 24-27). Joseph and Emma moved here in December 1827, first living with her parents (Joseph Smith-History 1:61-62).
The river where John the Baptist conferred the Aaronic Priesthood and where Peter, James and John appeared (D&C 128:20).
Harmony lay in Susquehanna County (D&C 128:20).
Early branch of the Church in Broome County (D&C 24:3; 26:1; 37:2).
Colesville lay in Broome County (D&C 128:20).
The Whitmer family farm, where the Church was organized in 1830 (D&C 14–18, 20–21, 28–30, 33–40).
Fayette lies in Seneca County (D&C 128:20–21).
The Smith family farm and the Sacred Grove (D&C 2, 19, 22, 23, 32).

Named in D&C 128:20. Joseph Smith-History 1:51-52 describes the hill near Manchester where the plates were buried but does not name it; Latter-day Saints began calling it Cumorah in Joseph Smith's lifetime, and he appears to have accepted the name late in his life (Smoot, Study Edition).
D&C 74 was given in Wayne County in 1830. The earliest source reads only "Wayne Co., NY, 1830", so the town and the month are not known.

Late in December 1830 Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon went from Fayette to Canandaigua to continue the Bible revision, and Joseph dictated D&C 37 there. The Church's headnote gives Fayette; the Joseph Smith Papers give Canandaigua Township.
D&C 100 was given at Perrysburg, Cattaraugus County, in 1833.

"The land Freedom and the regions round about" (D&C 106:1). Freedom, in Cattaraugus County, was the home of Warren A. Cowdery, whom the revelation called to preside over the church there (Joseph Smith Papers).
Named among the cities to be warned (D&C 84:114).
Named among the cities to be warned (D&C 84:114).
Named among the cities to be warned (D&C 84:114).
D&C 111 was given at Salem in 1836.
Hancock County settlement where D&C 130 and 131 were given in 1843. Joseph Smith stayed with Benjamin F. and Melissa LeBaron Johnson there in April 1843 (Joseph Smith Papers).
Formerly Commerce; Church headquarters 1839–46 (D&C 124–129, 132).
Where Joseph and Hyrum Smith were killed in Carthage Jail in 1844 (D&C 124:88; 135).
Named among the places to hear the proclamation (D&C 124:88).
Burlington, Iowa Territory, named among the places to hear the proclamation (D&C 124:88).
"Madison" in D&C 124:88 is Fort Madison, Iowa Territory (Joseph Smith Papers).

The settlement "upon the land opposite to the city of Nauvoo" named in D&C 125:3. It lay near Montrose, in Lee County; the exact site is uncertain. The branch had 326 members by August 1841 (Joseph Smith Papers).
Lee County settlement named in D&C 125:4. In January 1841 Joseph Smith told John Smith to "build up Nashville"; it had eighty members by August 1841 (Joseph Smith Papers).
"The saints in the Territory of Iowa" (D&C 125:1).
The state of Illinois (D&C 135:7).
D&C 138 and both Official Declarations were received or recorded here.
Named in Official Declaration 1.
The temple and Cache Stake Conference mentioned in Official Declaration 1.
Utah Territory and State (Official Declaration 1).
"The rebellion of South Carolina" (D&C 87:1; 130:12).
"The nation of Great Britain" (D&C 87:3). Placed at London.
D&C 29:41. The revelations do not say where it was; early Latter-day Saint teaching placed it in Jackson County, Missouri.
"The Mount of Transfiguration" (D&C 138:45). The mountain is not named in the Gospels; tradition says Mount Tabor, and Mount Hermon has also been proposed.
Joseph Smith's birthplace, 23 December 1805 (Joseph Smith-History 1:3).
Sharon lies in Windsor County (Joseph Smith-History 1:3).
The state of Vermont (Joseph Smith-History 1:3).

Joseph Smith Sr. moved to Palmyra in the summer of 1816 and the family followed that winter. Their log home (1818-19) stood in Palmyra Township just outside the village (Joseph Smith-History 1:3, 61, 64).
Palmyra and Manchester were in Ontario County; Palmyra is now in Wayne County (Joseph Smith-History 1:3, 51).
The state of New York.
The state of Pennsylvania.
Josiah Stowell lived in Chenango County (Joseph Smith-History 1:56, 58).
Where Joseph Smith was brought before a court in 1826 over his money-digging, and where he and Emma Hale were married in January 1827 (Joseph Smith-History 1:58).

The woods near the Smith home where Joseph Smith prayed in the spring of 1820 (Joseph Smith-History 1:14-17, 20). The text says only "the woods"; the forested land lay in Manchester Township, a little from the family's cabin in Palmyra Township, and is the site the Church has long identified.
